newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares pulled higher by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares pulled higher by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 2.02 percent as fresh foreign and domestic capital entered the market and investors sought shares in drug company Lek.
Traders said buying interest had been whetted by Lek's strong performance in recent weeks.
"Lek's newly listed shares have performed remarkably in the past three weeks. That is pulling the whole market up," one trader said.
He warned that the rally may run out of steam as Lek's progress slowed, however.
Since their listing three weeks ago, Lek's issue A shares have soared 39.2 percent.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 20.91 points to 1,057.43.
* 13 shares rose and seven fell, while four were untraded.
* Turnover jumped to 635.9 million tolars from 382.3 million.
* Lek's issue A was most actively traded, firming 0.66 percent to 19,165 tolars on volume of 15,290 shares for total turnover of 293 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, soaring 10 percent to 21,710 on volume of 12 shares for total turnover of 0.3 million tolars.

* Construction company GPG was the leading decliner. Its shares fell 2.39 percent to 7,321 on volume of 674 shares for total turnover of 4.9 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
